try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.title: Try it yourself: Center the inherited navigation on its main axis
try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The navigation is a flex row now, but its links still collect toward the start of the available horizontal space. Because the nav's main axis is horizontal, `justify-content` can reposition the whole group without editing individual links. Keep the Module 3 stylesheet and add `justify-content: center;` to a `nav` rule. Preview the header: the navigation group should sit centered along its row while the link styling stays intact.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for center the inherited navigation on its main axis so it reinforces Alignment, Distribution, and Gap.

try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.title: Try it yourself: Center header children on the cross axis
try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The header stacks vertically, but its children still do not share the same horizontal alignment. A column flex container has a horizontal cross axis, so `align-items` can center those children without changing their vertical order. Keep all prior rules and add `align-items: center;` to a `header` rule. Check the header: its existing children should align centrally across the `width` while remaining stacked.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for center header children on the cross axis so it reinforces Alignment, Distribution, and Gap.

try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.title: Try it yourself: Give navigation items consistent flex gap
try_alignment_distribution_and_gap_sketc.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The flex navigation needs spacing controlled by its parent instead of relying only on each link's own box. Gap belongs to the flex container and establishes a consistent rhythm between its children. Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `gap: 1rem;` to a `nav` rule. Preview the nav at a few widths: the links should have a clear, consistent flex spacing rhythm.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for give navigation items consistent flex gap so it reinforces Alignment, Distribution, and Gap.
